disease: General guide: field patterns, symptoms and signs of turf disease
institution_author: Purdue Extension, Richard Latin (BP-124-W, Dec. 2013)
symptoms_own_words: Explains how to tell turf diseases apart: patterns seen from a distance (circles, frog-eyes, rings, lines, diffuse areas), close-up symptoms (leaf spots, blight, dieback, rotten roots) and signs of the fungus itself. Stresses that many problems look alike and lab confirmation is often needed.
season: all year (chart of active months per disease, lower Midwest)

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Thinning turf that turns bright yellow, orange or bronze in irregular areas, starting as small yellow specks on golf greens. Up close the stem bases go black and tiny black hairy fruiting bodies appear.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Many small sunken copper or reddish-brown spots, up to about 3 inches, with tan centers, which look like ball marks. Mostly on new bentgrass or bermudagrass putting greens.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide
symptoms_own_words: Blackened, splotchy turf caused by slimy algae (cyanobacteria) growing on the thatch, which can form a crust. Usually in wet, shaded, poorly drained spots.
season: long warm, cloudy, rainy spells in summer and fall

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Round brown patches from a few inches to several feet across that appear almost overnight, sometimes with a dark grayish ring at the edge in the morning. Tall fescue leaves get chocolate-brown spots with darker borders.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo J. Kaminski
symptoms_own_words: Yellow rings from a few inches to over a foot wide, alone or in groups, often with darker green grass inside. Mainly on annual bluegrass greens.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Many small bleached or straw-colored spots (coin-sized on short turf, a few inches on lawns) that can merge into larger blighted areas. Leaves show tan lesions with brown or purple hourglass-shaped borders, and white cobweb-like threads in morning dew.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Circles or arcs of dark green, wilting or dead grass, sometimes with mushrooms or puffballs after rain. The fungus makes the soil repel water, so grass in the ring dries out.
season: early to mid summer; sometimes mild fall or winter

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: A ring of grass that is darker green and faster-growing than the grass around it, a few inches to many feet across, sometimes with mushrooms in wet weather. One type causes brown, drought-like rings on greens.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide
symptoms_own_words: Gray spots with yellow edges on ryegrass and tall fescue leaves with twisted gray tips; badly hit turf looks gray and drought-like and collapses fast. On warm-season grasses, oval brown spots with purple borders.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: After snow melts, round light-brown, gray or bleached matted patches up to about 2 feet, sometimes with gray fungal threads and tiny dark specks in the leaves.
season: winter; seen at snow melt after long snow cover

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Large reddish-brown to yellow rings and patches, from inches to many feet, often with an orange edge, on warm-season grasses such as zoysiagrass. Shows up as grass goes into or comes out of dormancy.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Reddish- or purplish-brown spots on leaves, sometimes with tan centers; when severe, leaves and shoots die and the stand thins and browns ("melting out").
season: mostly cool rainy spring and fall; some types in hot weather

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Small round reddish-brown, pink or tan spots without snow; under melting snow, larger round patches with tan centers and pinkish edges.
season: late fall to early spring, cold and wet; at snow melt

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Luke Dant
symptoms_own_words: Scalloped tan-to-orange rings about 4 to 18 inches across on bermudagrass greens, which may first look like drought or poor feeding.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo N. Tisserat
symptoms_own_words: Light-green spots that become thin round brown or straw-colored patches, often with live grass in the middle (frog-eye), on Kentucky bluegrass. Roots turn dark.
season: starts in moist spring; shows in summer heat and drought

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: A white powdery coating on leaves, as if dusted with lime; badly infected leaves yellow then brown, and shaded turf thins.
season: spring to fall, most in fall; shade

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Small yellow patches that turn into white fluffy growth on leaves and stems, later with small black dots; plants can be stunted. Written mainly for cereals and pasture grasses.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Dark, water-soaked spots that turn orange or bronze and quickly join into large dead areas, often along paths where water drains; leaves mat down and feel slimy, with fluffy gray threads in the morning.
season: hot humid summer nights after storms (cool-season grass)

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo L. Tredway
symptoms_own_words: Circles or irregular patches up to about 2 feet that first wilt or look underfed, then turn orange and collapse, on young bentgrass greens. Roots are short and tan.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Very variable: reddish-brown, blue-gray, purplish, yellow or bronze thinning patches that can look like wilt, on putting greens. The PDF says a lab test is usually needed to confirm it.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Pink or reddish spots and patches, from a couple of inches to a few feet; up close, red thread-like strands stick out of the leaves.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Yellow flecks on leaves that burst into orange or reddish-orange powder; from a distance the stand looks thin and yellow-orange, and the powder rubs off on shoes.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Scattered orange-red pustules on the top of leaves that can merge and later turn black. Written mainly for wheat and barley.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Blocky orange pustules on stems, leaves and sheaths that darken late in the season. Written mainly for wheat, oats and other cereal grasses.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo R. Smiley
symptoms_own_words: Stunted yellow-green plants whose leaves get long silvery-gray to black streaks, then split and shred; the stand looks thin and dry. On older Kentucky bluegrass types.
season: cool wet spring and fall, mostly spring

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide
symptoms_own_words: Sudden yellow, orange or reddish-brown circles, crescents or frog-eyes that grow quickly, with white threads at the edge and small mustard-brown balls on the soil.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide
symptoms_own_words: Bleached straw-colored round patches that stay dead when bermudagrass greens up in spring, sometimes with live grass in the center; roots are dark.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Kentucky bluegrass first looks thin or wilted, then gets round or irregular yellow-to-straw patches with bronze edges, sometimes with a live center (frog-eye).

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Pete Dernoeden, Ph.D.
symptoms_own_words: Small reddish-brown circles on bentgrass that become wilted blue-gray, red-brown or bronze patches up to several feet, often on new sand-based greens.
season: infects in cool wet spring/fall; shows in summer heat

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo Lane Tredway
symptoms_own_words: Patches or rings on warm-season grasses that first grow slowly and yellow, then turn tan or orange and die; roots and runners are rotten.

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide; photo S. McDonald
symptoms_own_words: Yellow rings a few inches to a foot or more across, sometimes reddish-brown rings that link together, on annual bluegrass and bentgrass greens; usually only cosmetic.
season: fall to spring, chilly and rainy

institution_author: Syngenta GreenCast disease guide
symptoms_own_words: Small yellow tufts (under an inch) of crowded shoots that pull out easily, showing short stubby roots, mostly on greens. On St. Augustinegrass, white streaks along the leaves instead.
season: cloudy periods, mostly late fall to spring

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Leaf spots with a red border and gray center, from pin-prick to long, on leaves, sheaths and crowns; infected leaves yellow and die.
season: cool wet weather; also under drought stress

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Small oval water-soaked spots that turn brown with yellow edges and merge into long brown streaks, sometimes with ooze. Bacterial, written mainly for cereals and pasture grasses.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Leaf tips turn yellow, then purple or red, in small patches of a field. A virus spread by aphids, written for barley, wheat and other cereals.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Dark hard bodies replace seeds in flowering grass heads, after a sticky "honeydew" stage; no other visible leaf symptoms. Matters for seed heads, not mowed turf.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Small yellow spots that become long tan-orange blotches with tiny black dots in the middle, moving up the plant. Written mainly for wheat.

institution_author: SDSU Extension (Lagerhausen, Strunk, Tande, Shires) - Grass Diseases of South Dakota
symptoms_own_words: Purple spots and blotches on leaves and dark purple-to-black seed husks. Written for wheat, barley and rye.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, David Graper
symptoms_own_words: Cool-season lawns turn brown and go dormant-like in hot dry weather, often looking patchy because the grass mix varies; the grass usually greens up again once it gets water.

disease: White grubs (May/June beetle, masked chafer, Japanese beetle)
pdf_file: insect_damage/Do You Have Grubs in Your Lawn_.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Grubs eat the roots, so grass wilts, turns light brown then brown, and can be rolled back like carpet; animals may dig it up looking for grubs. Check by digging at the edge of the dead patch.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Leo Schleicher
symptoms_own_words: Turf turns brown and dies like drought because roots are eaten, and lifts up in sections showing C-shaped white grubs; skunks, moles and birds may tear it up.

pdf_file: insect_damage/What Are These Shiny Beetles in My Yard and Why Are They Eating Everything_.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Shiny adult beetles skeletonize leaves of garden plants; their grubs eat grass roots, causing brown and then dead patches of lawn.
season: adults mid-summer; grubs late July to mid-August

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Small round brown patches, about 2 to 10 inches, where caterpillars clip grass blades at the soil at night; grass usually regrows unless already stressed.

pdf_file: insect_damage/Monitor Lawns and Gardens for Bronzed Cutworm Activity.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Caterpillar feeding leaves small brown circular spots in lawns; large numbers can badly injure a lawn.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Patrick Wagner et al.
symptoms_own_words: Larvae chew grass blades, so the lawn looks thin and drought-stressed or gets dead patches when severe; this species usually does little harm.

pdf_file: insect_damage/What Are the Little Moths All Over My Lawn_.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Patrick Wagner et al.
symptoms_own_words: Small ragged brown patches that look scalped, sometimes with silk tubes or webbing; over time the lawn can look thin with several dead patches, worse in hot drought.
season: spring to fall; moths in summer

pdf_file: insect_damage/What’s Leaving These White Skins on My Lawn_.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: White tube-like silk liners with dark ends lying on the lawn (left by birds that ate the larvae); feeding can cause brown patches.

pdf_file: insect_damage/Drought Conditions Magnifying Impact of Black Grass Bugs.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Patrick Wagner et al.
symptoms_own_words: Tiny black bugs suck on grass, leaving many small pale or white speckles on the leaves; worst on wheatgrass pastures in drought.

pdf_file: insect_damage/Grasshoppers_ When to Manage Them in a Yard and Garden.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Article is about grasshoppers chewing gardens, shrubs and small trees in dry years; it does not describe lawn symptoms.

pdf_file: insect_damage/Giant Wasps Are Invading My Yard! No, They Still Aren’t Murder Hornets_.pdf
institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Large wasps dig burrows in bare, dry or sandy soil and leave small mounds of dug-out soil; they do not harm grass much.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Adam Varenhorst et al.
symptoms_own_words: Loud insects in trees; nymphs live in the soil feeding on tree roots and leave empty skins on trunks. No turf symptoms described.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Leo Schleicher
symptoms_own_words: A spongy layer of dead stems and roots thicker than about half an inch between soil and green grass; it repels water and can cause dry spots and scalping.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Paul O. Johnson (rev.), Moechnig, Deneke, Andersen (2018)
symptoms_own_words: Lists common perennial and annual lawn weeds and which weed killers control them. Weeds, not a turf disease.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Paul O. Johnson
symptoms_own_words: Yellow dandelion flowers spread across lawns in cool damp spring weather. A weed, not a turf disease.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Paul O. Johnson
symptoms_own_words: About controlling dandelion, ground ivy, bindweed, creeping bellflower and white clover in fall. Weeds, not a turf disease.

institution_author: SDSU Extension, Paul O. Johnson
symptoms_own_words: Short page saying a dense healthy lawn is the best defense against weeds; links a download. No symptoms described.
